title: Find the warmed can in a chilled delivery with a slow, jittery thermometer
instruction: One of these three chilled cans from the same delivery has warmed up. Find the warmest can with the thermometer and put it on the red reject mat, then let go. A can is measured while it stands on the grey plate and is not held; the display beside the plate shows the reading in degrees C.
context: Shipping and receiving clerks (O*NET 43-5071) and food service managers (11-9051) check refrigerated deliveries with a contact or probe thermometer before accepting them; the FDA Food Code requires refrigerated food to arrive at 5 C (41 F) or colder. These thermometers take seconds to settle and their readings jitter, so a quick look at each item ranks them by the order they were checked. Passing the warmed item lets bacteria grow in food that will be sold.
setup: Station table, top 0.7475 m above the floor. Positions in metres in the robots' frame: x forward from the line through the two arm bases (at y +0.305 and -0.305), y to the robots' left; heights above the table top. (1) Three sealed tinplate steel food cans, loose and identical: 73 mm across, 110 mm tall, 450 g each (full of water), plain steel finish (0.78, 0.79, 0.80), friction 0.9, standing upright in a line on the robots' left at y 0.15, 8.5 cm apart. Each has a 22 mm square coloured dot printed on its lid: blue (0.15, 0.35, 0.85) at (0.20, 0.15), green (0.15, 0.65, 0.25) at (0.285, 0.15), yellow (0.95, 0.80, 0.10) at (0.37, 0.15). (2) The thermometer's sensing plate, fixed: grey (0.55, 0.56, 0.58) anodised aluminium, 10 x 10 cm, 4 mm thick, centred at (0.25, 0.00). (3) Its display, loose but heavy (6 kg): a grey (0.20, 0.20, 0.22) box 8 x 13 x 4 cm (13 cm along y) centred at (0.38, 0.00), just beyond the plate, with a dark screen on top showing three red (1.0, 0.12, 0.08) 7-segment digits 4.5 cm tall, decimal point before the last digit, a leading zero left blank, the tops of the digits away from the robots so they read upright from the robots' side. It reads about 22 (room temperature) at the start and updates every 0.5 s. (4) A red (0.80, 0.12, 0.10) reject mat, fixed, 12 x 12 cm, 2 mm thick, centred at (0.30, -0.16). No other objects.
scoring: From the trial's record of every display update (time, value, and which can stood on the plate untouched) and the end state; a real trial is scored from a video of the plate and display and a top photo at the end. A can is measured while it stands upright on the plate (its base inside the plate's square) and neither gripper's TCP is within 9 cm of the can's centre. Settled readings: in each run of consecutive updates with one can measured, the readings from the earliest point where straight-line fits through the next 12 readings and through all the rest of the run both have slopes within 2 standard errors of zero (none if there is no such point). Proof: every can has settled readings, and the warmest can's mean settled reading exceeds each other can's by more than 3 standard errors of the difference, with the SD pooled from every settled reading's scatter about its own can's mean. Gates, each gives 0: at any time a can leans more than 30 degrees or falls off the table, or the display box moves more than 1 cm; at the end, any can other than the warmest stands on the mat. Otherwise the score at the end is the highest rung reached: 0.5 if the settled readings prove the warmest can (settled readings without a proof score 0); 0.75 if that can also stands upright and alone on the mat (base inside its square); 1.0 (success, held 1 s) if also neither gripper's TCP is within 9 cm of it and it is at rest. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the cans back at their spots, refill or re-chill so the warmed can and the others are at their temperatures, and let the plate return to room temperature (the display reads about 22.0). In simulation the temperatures come from the trial seed (WARMCUP_SEED, default 0); object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz; the cans are rigid cylinders at real size and mass (no slosh). The thermometer is code: the plate's sensor follows the measured can as a first-order lag (time constant 4 s) and relaxes toward 22 C when the plate is empty or the can is held; each 0.5 s update adds Gaussian noise (SD 0.8 C) and rounds to 0.1 C. Hidden can temperatures: the warmed can 6.0 to 9.0 C, each other can 1.5 to 2.0 C below the next; cans do not change temperature during a trial. A real receiving check probes between packages; the plate stands in for the probe. The display's lit segments are shown or hidden by code; for about the first second after a reset it shows 88.8 until its first update renders.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (6,000 steps, seed 0); demo: 1.0 (success at step 4,027, seed 0)
